MCD.rationale: MCD presents a mildly attractive fundamental case. The franchise model is elite — 95% franchised, 45.2% operating margin, 89.6% gross margin, and 30.4% net margin in Q1 2026, all stable. YoY revenue grew +9.4% and EPS diluted +6.9%, demonstrating the business is expanding. Cash conversion is strong at 122% (OCF $2.41B vs net income $1.98B). The balance sheet is structurally negative-equity but improving by $2.16B over four quarters. The stock is down -16.9% from its February high and sits within 2.2% of its 52-week low, while fundamentals are advancing — a notable divergence. The qual report cites an external P/E of 23, the lowest in nearly two years, and analyst consensus of 35% upside. However, the pack's own valuation data is corrupted (pe_diluted=0 across all observations), so I cannot independently confirm the discount magnitude. Macro headwinds are real: oil at $92.65 (+30% in 90 days) pressures franchisee costs, and the 10Y yield at 4.45% (+40bps) raises refinancing risk on $61.3B in liabilities. CEO commentary on weakening consumer spending among lower-income families is a near-term traffic risk. The refranchising of U.S. company-owned locations and the 210M loyalty-user digital platform are structural positives. Net: strong franchise quality and positive trajectory, but macro cost headwinds, consumer softness, and unverifiable valuation cap the score at mildly positive. No strong near-term catalyst beyond potential refranchising announcement.

With over 45,300 total systemwide locations as of FY2025, near 95% franchised, McDonald's collects high-margin royalties (typically 4-5% of sales) plus rent, generating an FY2025 operating margin of 46.1%... Its loyalty platform now reaches ~210 million 90-day active users

McDonald's Corporation reported solid first-quarter 2026 growth... Total revenues rose to $6.52 billion... operating income 12% to $2.95 billion, supported by 3.8% global comparable sales growth and a 45.3% operating margin.
McDonald's stock has fallen 20% from February highs... Trading at a P/E ratio of 23 (lowest in nearly two years)... analysts see 35% upside potential.

McDonald's CEO says consumer spending could be 'getting a little bit worse'... its company-owned restaurants... have been seeing weaker margins, so McDonald's is considering selling them to franchisees.
Risks: (1) franchisee tension over royalty rate... (2) California-style minimum wage spread... (3) commodity inflation cycle on beef/eggs... but royalty income is sales-based not margin-based.
